column1: # Wire, connector, crimp-tool and heat-shrink BOM, refreshed 2026-10-12 against control-system-bom.csv, module-interconnect.csv and mains-inlet-protection.md. control-system-bom.csv and part-numbers.csv cover ICs/modules/sensors/actuators but carry no wire/connector/tool line items. Sized against the branch currents established in this directory: heater branches 4.36A (coffee) and 4.89A (steam) at 230V, rising to 4.80A and 5.38A at 253V (the BOM's 4.80A and 5.38A are the 253V figures; computed from the measured 52.7 ohm and 47.0 ohm element resistances), so up to ~5.4A continuous at 253V when firing AND physically near an SSR dissipating ~5-6.5W (SSR mounting is proposed, not decided: try mounting direct to the metal side wall instead of heatsinks, no source says the wall is earthed; either way the run is warm, so ordinary PVC insulation is not appropriate); pump branches 0.1-0.22A (BOM) and valve coils 5-9W (BOM), so low actual current but still mains-rated insulation; the mains trunk from the IEC inlet through the T10A fuse must be rated at or above the fuse rating for the fuse to protect the wire that matters (rating margin of the trunk and valve branches is an OPEN DECISION, see mains-inlet-protection.md); 5V DC distribution has a typical-based budget of about 0.53A (many items estimated, unmeasured; about 0.66-0.86A with the VID6608 datasheet maximum, see mains-inlet-protection.md) against the Mean Well IRM-10-5's 2A (1.5A at 60C ambient, 1.0A at 70C, derated); signal wiring (GPIO/UART/I2C/SPI) is <20mA per line and gauge there is about handling/solderability, not current. AU-sourced to match this project's existing supplier pattern (Jaycar/Altronics/Core Electronics/element14 AU/RS AU, AliExpress only where nothing local exists). Rows marked 'to confirm' in the Confidence column are not resolvable from the design files and are listed in _carry-forward/heater-mains-wiring.md.

column1: Signal hookup wire (GPIO/UART/I2C/SPI)
column2: Jaycar WH3009 - Light Duty Hook-up Wire Pack 8 colours
column6: 26AWG (13/0.12mm) 0.6A-rated - current headroom is irrelevant here (<20mA/line), the gauge is chosen for handling and solderability on perfboard. 8 colours useful for tracing ~40+ connections. Dimmer Z-C/DIM logic wiring: keep under 30cm (vendor), twist Z-C with GND, away from AC runs, ferrite on the cable if dimming is erratic (module-interconnect). Do NOT connect the BL0942 UART/VCC/GND wiring to the controller until the module's isolation has been measured (BL0942 is mains-referenced). Near the hot blocks the temperature rating of this PVC-class wire is not stated in the inputs - to confirm before running it beside the thermoblocks

column1: 5V DC distribution wire (PSU to board / relay coils / dimmer logic)
column2: 22AWG tinned stranded hookup wire
column6: Typical-based 5V budget about 0.53A (many items estimated, unmeasured; about 0.66-0.86A with the VID6608 datasheet maximum, up to ~86% of the 1.0A available at 70C) against the IRM-10-5's 2A (1.5A at 60C ambient, 1.0A at 70C) - 22AWG gives comfortable margin. An earlier note quoted ~450mA 'measured' against a 1A max; that figure left out the panel, gauge board and buzzer and is superseded. Landing method (screw terminal or crimp) is a build-time choice, not a wire-spec question

column1: DuPont crimp kit + tool
column2: IWISS SN-28B ratcheting crimper + connector/housing kit
column3: AliExpress / Amazon AU (no AU bricks-and-mortar stocks a bundled kit)
column6: MUST be the ratcheting SN-28B, not the flat pliers-style knockoff sold under the same name - check listings explicitly say 'ratchet'. Covers 28-18AWG at 2.54mm/3.96mm pitch (DuPont and JST-XH). Core Electronics stocks genuine Pololu 2.54mm housings/pins locally (POLOLU-1900) if a partial-local-sourcing split is preferred over one AliExpress order. Module-side connections that use it (module-interconnect): relay module VCC/GND/IN1-IN4, ULN2003A breakout IN1/IN2/GND, dimmer GND/VCC/Z-C/DIM headers (3V3 supply, never 12V), 74HCT541 gauge lines, XDB401 I2C if the sensors are not hard-wired. The 10k pull-downs at the ULN2003A and dimmer headers and the relay-input pull resistors are fitted at the module end, so the wire from the controller can be disconnected without un-holding the load

column1: Mains flex - pump/valve branches (0.75mm2 class, 250V)
column2: Jaycar WB1562 - Flexible Three Core Mains Cable
column6: 3-core (Active/Neutral/Earth), 250VAC round PVC flex described as 10A-class. OPEN DECISION: inlet chain rating margin - the real rating of 0.75mm2 cord must be checked against the applicable standard (a reviewer believes it is commonly 7.5A in AU, unverified), and these valve branches carry no branch fuse, so the T10A may not protect them. Fine for pump/valve branches where actual current is low (pump 0.1-0.22A, valve coil 5-9W) but insulation rating still matters. Each pump branch carries a 1-2A slow-blow fuse in the dimmer's AC-L in feed, which protects the thin pump leads (the T10A trunk fuse does not). PVC temperature rating near the hot thermoblock and the 140C-class valves is not stated in the inputs - to confirm

column1: Mains trunk - inlet to fuse to distribution (must match T10A fuse rating)
column2: Jaycar WB1565 - Mains 10A Twin and Earth Power Cable
column6: 1.0mm2, 250VAC, 10A - chosen to match the T10A slow-blow fuse rating (OPEN DECISION: a cable rated equal to its fuse is not protection once derating is allowed for; see mains-inlet-protection.md). WB1568 (20A/2mm2) is a fine upgrade if extra margin is wanted and cheap enough to justify. Cable rating (10A) equals the T10A fuse, which is the minimum for the fuse to protect it. reference-machine.md puts the machine's own worst case at about 9.95A at 240V and 10.5A at 253V, so the 10A trunk, the T10A fuse and the FN9222 (10A at 50C) all sit at that figure - sizing against the worst case and in-enclosure derating of the cable is to confirm. OPEN DECISION: inlet chain rating margin - a cable rated equal to its fuse is not protection once enclosure derating and a slow-blow fuse's long-time overload band are allowed for; the FN9222 is 10A at 50C; owner to decide, parts unchanged (see mains-inlet-protection.md)

column1: Heater branch wire (up to ~5.4A continuous at 253V, near an SSR - HIGH TEMP REQUIRED)
column2: Core Electronics FIT0584 - 16AWG (1.5mm2) High-Temperature Silicone Wire
column6: -60C to +200C silicone, tinned copper, correctly gauged and rated for the load next to the SSR heatsink's 5-6W dissipation. DO NOT substitute Jaycar WH3037 ('7.5A Heavy Duty Silicone') - it is 180C but only ~0.75mm2/18AWG and Jaycar itself rates it at only 7.5A, too close to the up-to-5.4A continuous load (253V) for comfort next to a hot SSR. DO NOT substitute Altronics W2291 ('high temperature hook up cable') - despite the name it is only 105C-rated PVC, not silicone/PTFE, and does not meet the requirement. FIT0583 (14AWG/2.5mm2) is the step-up if more thermal/current margin is wanted. Heater load figures: coffee 4.36A and steam 4.89A at 230V, 4.80A and 5.38A at 253V (the BOM's figures are the 253V ones); each branch is switched by an EARU SSR-40DA whose load terminals are screw terminals (module-interconnect). The high-temperature requirement stands whether or not the SSR gets a heatsink (SSR mounting is proposed, not decided: try mounting direct to the metal side wall per the BOM user note; no source says the wall is earthed; the SSR dissipates ~5-6.5W against the IRM-10-5 derating from 100% at 50C), since the SSR dissipates ~5-6W either way

column1: Crimp tool - insulated terminals
column2: Jaycar TH1829 - Heavy Duty Ratchet Crimping Tool for Insulated Terminals
column6: Genuine ratcheting mechanism (will not release until full crimp) - not the cheap pliers-style tool. 0.5-6.0mm2 range, colour-keyed jaws (red/blue/yellow). Alt: Altronics T2177 Crimptool Ratchet Multi-Connector Universal Kit

column1: Crimp terminals - ring/spade/fork
column2: Jaycar PT4530 - Quick Connect Crimp Connector Pack (160pc)
column6: 6.35mm/4.8mm/3.3mm quick-disconnect spades plus assorted ring/butt types, colour-keyed to TH1829's jaws. Match barrel colour to gauge: red = 0.5-1.5mm2 (covers the 0.75mm2 pump/valve branches and the 1.0mm2 mains trunk), blue = 1.5-2.5mm2 (covers the 1.5mm2 heater branches) - 1.5mm2 appears in both ranges, use blue for it; do not crimp a 1.5mm2 conductor in a red barrel or a 0.75mm2 or 1.0mm2 conductor loose in a blue one. Ferrules for stranded conductors in the SSR, dimmer and PCB screw terminals are not specified anywhere in the BOM or module-interconnect - to confirm

column1: Heat shrink - general low-voltage strain relief
column2: Jaycar WH5525 - Assorted Heatshrink Pack 1.5-10mm (or WH5520 Ultimate Heatshrink Pack)
column6: Standard 2:1 polyolefin assortment - fine for perfboard/DuPont-side strain relief. NOT rated or intended for mains joints - see next row

column1: Heat shrink - MAINS-rated adhesive-lined joints
column2: RS PRO Adhesive Lined Heat Shrink Tube 3:1 ratio
column3: RS Australia (also element14 AU under 3M/Pro Power/Raychem ATUM)
column6: 6.4/9/12.7mm diameters, ~1.2m lengths, MIL-DTL-23053/4 Class 3 / UL224, 125C / 600V - comfortably covers the 300V+ mains-joint requirement. Jaycar's own glue-lined heatshrink (WH5643, 4:1) is a lower-ratio water/dust-resistant product only, not explicitly voltage-rated - use it for low-voltage sealing, not mains joints

column1: Mains distribution / daisy-chain - lever-connector option
column2: Wago 221-412 (2-way lever connector) + 221-500 DIN mounting carrier
column3: Cutter Electronics / element14 AU / K&A Electronics
column6: 32A/450V per Wago datasheet WHEN mounted in the 221-500 carrier per spacing; free-hanging/unspaced the safe figure is closer to 275V - still well over the 240V/10A need either way, but MUST be seated in the carrier for proper strain relief and mechanical fixing, not left loose. Tool-less, fast, reusable, good with fine-strand appliance flex. Genuine Wago carries ENEC/VDE/UL/CSA approval, recognised under AS/NZS 3000:2018

column1: Mains distribution / daisy-chain - DIN rail terminal block option (RECOMMENDED for the permanent distribution point)
column2: Dinkle DIN rail terminal blocks (+ end clamp/end cap)
column3: Altronics (dinkle range) / Weidmuller or Phoenix Contact via element14 AU
column6: Standard UL-approved panel-building practice - positive mechanical DIN-rail mounting gives materially better vibration resistance than a free-floating lever connector (relevant here: pump vibration, thermal cycling from the SSR), clear per-terminal marking for inspection, screw clamp gives visible/tactile torque confirmation, easily isolated per-circuit for fault-finding. Needs the DIN rail itself mounted in the enclosure and periodic re-torque check on stranded conductors. This is the more standard/inspectable choice for the PERMANENT mains distribution point given this build's existing servicing-isolation theme; Wago 221s (above) are a legitimate faster-to-build alternative

column1: Mains joints - twist + tape / twist + heatshrink [NOT ACCEPTABLE - do not use]
column2: N/A
column6: NOT acceptable practice for a permanent appliance mains joint. No listed/tested approval for the purpose (unlike Wago 221 or a proper terminal block - no AS/NZS 60998-type approval as a connector). Relies on friction/twist geometry not rated for vibration + thermal cycling. Heat shrink over a twist provides insulation only, not mechanical retention - contact pressure is not maintained as copper cold-flows/relaxes over time, no strain relief, and the joint is not inspectable without destroying the sleeve. Wire nuts are a fixed-building-wiring fitting (undisturbed, in a wall cavity), not an appliance-internal fitting subject to pump vibration and SSR thermal cycling. Use the Wago/DIN-terminal-block rows above, OR the genuinely-crimped closed-end connector row below, for every permanent mains joint in this build instead

column1: Mains joints - crimped closed-end connector [ACCEPTABLE for permanent non-serviceable splices only]
column2: RS PRO Insulated Closed End Connector, 1.25mm2 (22-16AWG) and 1.5-2.5mm2 (16-14AWG) ranges; also TE Connectivity/AMP 321-series End Splice, 300V rated
column4: varies - verify current AU stock/price at checkout
column5: medium - part numbers traced to manufacturer catalogue but live AU stock/price not confirmed
column6: THIS is what an OEM 'twisted and crimped' joint actually is - NOT the same as the twist+tape row above. A closed-end connector is a barrel closed at one end; all conductors enter the open end, get twisted together, and a SINGLE crimp compresses the whole bundle into a gas-tight metal-to-metal joint (the crimp plastically cold-flows the copper - this is why it needs no service access and is trusted in automotive/aerospace harnesses with zero rework). Do NOT search 'B-connector' at AU retailers - that term surfaces Jaycar's HP1214/HP1270/HP1272, which are gel-filled insulation-piercing LOW-VOLTAGE telecom/alarm splices, not mains-rated and the wrong product. Crimped with the SAME indent/oval jaw as the insulated butt-splice profile already on the Jaycar TH1829 ratchet crimper above - no new tool is strictly required, BUT multi-wire (3-4 conductor) caps have a fatter barrel than a 2-wire splice in the same colour class, so physically check the connector's rated barrel diameter against the TH1829's jaw opening before trusting a real joint - a cosmetically-closed crimp that didn't fully seat is not gas-tight. A dedicated RS PRO multi-cavity closed-end ratchet crimper exists as a fallback if the TH1829 doesn't fit. SERVICEABILITY CAVEAT: this joint is destructive to undo, same as any crimp terminal - use it ONLY for joints genuinely permanent and buried in the harness (matching the OEM precedent). Anything that might need rework during debugging keeps using the Wago/DIN-terminal-block rows above instead
